title: Code on Wages: minimum wage, floor wage and timely payment
author: Editorial Desk
summary: What the Code on Wages, 2019 changes for ordinary workers.
body:
The **Code on Wages, 2019** is the first of the four Labour Codes passed by Parliament. It is built around three ideas.

## Universal minimum wage

Under the older Minimum Wages Act, only workers in "scheduled employments" were covered. The Code extends the right to a minimum wage to **all employees**, organised and unorganised.

## A national floor wage

The Code allows the Central Government to fix a **floor wage**, taking into account the living standards of workers. State minimum wages cannot be set below it. The idea is to stop a race to the bottom between States.

## One definition of wages

The Code gives a single definition of "wages". Allowances and other components are counted, with a cap on what can be excluded, so that employers do not keep basic pay low in order to reduce their contributions towards provident fund and gratuity.

## Time-bound payment

The Code requires wages to be paid on time and sets out the due dates by wage period. It also provides for equal remuneration for men and women and for transgender persons for the same or similar work.

## Questions workers ask

- Will my State's minimum wage fall? The Code says the floor wage is a floor, not a ceiling.
- Who enforces it? Inspector-cum-facilitators, the appropriate Government and, in the end, courts and tribunals.

BMS has long demanded a **need-based minimum wage**, in line with the principles laid down by the Indian Labour Conference.
